evidence_items.explanation: On a benchmark built to test general learning in unfamiliar settings, frontier AI scored far below ordinary humans in March 2026. That is inconsistent with AGI having been achieved.

evidence_items.locator: paragraph after 'In brief', second paragraph of body

receipt.public_excerpt: Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro led the pack at 0.37%. OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 came in at 0.26%. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 managed 0.25%, while xAI’s Grok-4.20 scored exactly zero. Humans, meanwhile, solved 100% of environments.

evidence_items.explanation: Each leading lab's frontier model of March 2026 scored under 1% on tasks humans fully solved. This supports the view that no general human-level system existed.

receipt.public_excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang went on Lex Fridman's podcast last week and said, plainly, "I think we've achieved AGI."

evidence_items.explanation: A prominent industry figure claimed AGI had been achieved in March 2026. This is an opinion, not a broadly accepted declaration, but it shows the claim is contested.

unresolved_gaps: There is no agreed definition of AGI, so 'not achieved' rests on the plain reading and benchmark evidence.
The original Forbes interview in which Altman reportedly said OpenAI had 'basically built AGI' and Nadella disagreed could not be read directly.
